answer: To resist sybil attacks, we deploy Stake-Bonded TPM Attestation. First, an agent must register a unique hardware kernel signature via a secure enclave. Second, the agent stakes $5,000 in tokens into a mesa-like liquidity pool for escrow. Third, the network verifies the hardware identity against a distributed relic of validated nodes. An attacker attempting to forge ten fake identities would face a $50,000 bond cost and 72 hours of compute verification. This mechanism acts like a heavy iron seal on a royal scroll, ensuring only the one true, singular sender can ever claim authority.
